- DHCP Server & DNS Forwarder to cloud resolver (CC-LNK-04)
- Traffic shaping: Operational priority; non-op capped 2/0.5 Mbps
- Egress: 2x IPsec VPN tunnels (IKEv2 UDP 500 / NAT-T UDP 4500, CC-LNK-01/03)
- Local Breakout: Direct internet exit for guests & yard; bypasses IPsec tunnel
- Resilience: Primary 100 Mbps WAN (10.4x.20.2) + Cellular backup router (10.4x.20.3)

div.div:
FLOW 1: FARM (CROP ZONE)
Actor & Device: Crop node, energy autonomous (solar+battery, ASM-070)
Exit Protocol: MQTT 3.1.1/5 over TLS 1.2+, X.509 client cert, port 8883 (443 ALPN alt), QoS 1
Local Buffer: Non-volatile ring buffer, max retention 24 hours (ASM-074)
Without Signal: Store-and-forward; on reconnect, live reading sent first, then oldest drained
Cloud Endpoint: AWS IoT Core regional endpoint in us-east-1, public (D09)
Alert Path: IoT Rule -> SQS -> Threshold Lambda (D10) -> SNS -> Farmer Phone (<5 min, 210 s target)
Bypasses Collection Center and VPC subnets (telemetry_ingress is reserved for interface endpoints).

div.div:
FLOW 2: FARM OUT OF COVERAGE
Actor & Device: Crop & drying nodes with dual-mode cellular + satellite module (ASM-073)
Exit Protocol: Same MQTT over TLS with X.509 cert over satellite IP bearer
Local Buffer: Same 24 h non-volatile buffer; contact interval <= 4 hours
Without Signal: Readings wait in buffer for next satellite contact pass (within 24 h)
Cloud Endpoint: Same AWS IoT Core regional endpoint and topic in us-east-1 (No cloud redesign)
Farmer Alert: Alert raised in cloud on contact; reaches farmer when phone enters data coverage
Opens drone confirmation case immediately (crop_alert_raised) without waiting for farmer.

div.div:
FLOW 3: WET MILL (DRYING & SACKS)
Actor & Device: Drying node (hourly reading); Farmer smartphone & app
Exit Protocol: Drying node: MQTT over TLS (same as farm). Farmer app: HTTPS TLS 1.2+
Local Buffer: Drying node: 24 h buffer. Farmer app: Encrypted outbox until persistence ACK (ASM-079)
Without Signal: Drying: Store-and-forward 24 h. Farmer app: Outbox holds sack registration
Cloud Endpoint: Drying -> IoT Core. Farmer app -> CloudFront / Public App API -> application tier
Custody Resilience: Transporter can accept custody by scanning sack even if farm upload is delayed.

div.div:
FLOW 4: CONTRACTED DRONE OPERATOR
Actor & Device: Contracted operator drone and ground station (ADR-002, ASM-023)
Exit Protocol: HTTPS TLS 1.2+; Mission download via API; Flight record & imagery upload to S3
Local Buffer: Storage of drone and ground station; no time limit; fumigation cannot close until persisted
Without Signal: Mission preloaded; flight proceeds; record/objects buffered until reconnect
Path from Center: Ground station on Soporte (10.4x.2.10) -> IPsec VPN -> transit -> application & object_storage S3 interface endpoints (CC-DRN-01/03). (drone_object_ingress tier holds no endpoint in pilot, ASM-140!)
Path from Municipal Seat: Public data link -> Public internet -> Public S3 (presigned URL) & API.

div.div:
FLOW 5: TRANSPORTER EN ROUTE & YARD
Actor & Device: Transporter smartphone and mobile app (ASM-076, ASM-079)
Exit Protocol: HTTPS TLS 1.2+; GNSS fix every 5 min en route; transport_position & sack_custody
Local Buffer: Encrypted outbox (7 days capacity, 2,016 fixes); custody events never evicted
Without Signal: GNSS fixes continue without data; on reconnect, custody uploaded first, then positions
Cloud Endpoint: CloudFront / Public Application API -> application tier
Collection Center Yard: Optional connection to cc-transport SSID (10.4x.4.0/24); uses local internet breakout directly to Public API; does NOT traverse the IPsec VPN tunnel (CC-TEL-02).

div.div:
FLOW 6: COLLECTION CENTER WAN & OPERATIONS
Actor & Device: Logistics reception posts, desktops, code-sheet printers, and center firewall
Exit Protocol: IPsec site-to-site VPN (2 tunnels over 100 Mbps WAN + cellular backup, ASM-078)
Local Buffer: Encrypted outbox on each logistics post; releases on persistence ACK (ASM-079)
Without WAN: Reception continues offline; events buffer locally; RADIUS validates via cached CRL
Cloud Endpoint: Hub -> transit tier -> pdn application (CC-LOG-01) & administration (CC-ADM-01/02)
Printing & Breakout: Code sheets print locally on VLAN 110 (CC-LOG-02); Guest/yard break out to web.

div.div:
FLOW 7: PORT OF BUENAVENTURA
Actor & Device: Transporter smartphone and app (ASM-077); No Federation equipment deployed
Exit Protocol: HTTPS TLS 1.2+ over public cellular network
Local Buffer: Transporter app encrypted outbox; keeps original recorded_at timestamp
Without Signal: Event waits in outbox; uploads on data reconnect
Cloud Endpoint: CloudFront / Public Application API -> application tier
Event Recorded: sack_custody with outcome=accepted/rejected and receiver reference; closes trip.

[D05] Center Association: 10.40.0.0/13 summary, IPsec VPN tunnels, TGW Hub in Network Acct
[D07] Pattern Firewall Rules: Center firewall (CC rules) & VPC security controls (CL rules)
[D08] Reusable Farm Module: Pattern farm crop/drying nodes, 24 h buffer, satellite dual-mode
[D09] Telemetry Ingestion: AWS IoT Core regional endpoint, mutual X.509, idempotent DynamoDB
[D10] Event-Driven Inference: Threshold Lambda, SQS queue, SNS alert pipeline (<5 min budget)
Azure: 10.88.0.0/13 Prepared, not deployed secondary cloud export target (ADR-001).

div.div:
ARCHITECTURAL CONTRACT & DESIGN PRINCIPLES (docs/connectivity.md Section 2):
1. Identity, Not Address: Field devices and phones hold no cloud private IP; authenticated by X.509 certs or IAM/Cognito. Scaling from 200 to 1,000 farms needs no re-addressing.
2. Bearer Neutrality: IP bearer carrying TLS only; no dependency on 2G/3G or legacy circuit-switched mobile generations (ASM-072, PD-080).
3. Original Timestamp & Idempotency: Every buffered record carries creation time and idempotency key (node_id + timestamp or event_id). Drained record evaluated as if live.
4. Release on Acknowledgement: Records leave local buffer ONLY after verified cloud ACK (MQTT PUBACK, HTTP 2xx, or S3 checksum). Duplicate delivery is harmlessly absorbed.
5. End-to-End Encryption: TLS 1.2+ end-to-end; no intermediate gateway terminates TLS or inspects payloads. Buffers encrypted at rest.

div.div:
CROP ALERT LATENCY BUDGET BREAKDOWN (< 5 MINUTES / 300 SECONDS CASE STATEMENT TARGET) - docs/connectivity.md Section 8.2:
Hop 1: Reading taken to message ready on node (10 s) --> Hop 2: Radio wake, network attach & TLS connection (60 s) --> Hop 3: MQTT publish to broker PUBACK at IoT Core (20 s) --> Hop 4: Topic rule to SQS threshold queue invocation (10 s)
Hop 5: Threshold Lambda evaluates ranges, writes DB & publishes SNS (20 s) --> Hop 6: SNS topic to notification provider (30 s) --> Hop 7: Provider to Farmer Phone (60 s) | TOTAL TARGET: 210 s | MARGIN: 90 s | CASE LIMIT: 300 s

div.div:
NORMATIVE REFERENCES & REPOSITORY BOUNDARIES (aroma-pacifico-diagrams network/):
- Source documents: docs/connectivity.md (all sections), docs/collection-center-network.md, docs/firewall-policy.md section 4 in aroma-pacifico-architecture (main).
- Traceability to IaC: Box catalog in docs/architecture.md section 14 (D04 VPC/Tiers, D05 Center Association, D07 Firewall Rules, D08 Farm Module, D09 Telemetry, D10 Inference Functions).
- Strict No-Signal Constraints: Telemetry buffer max 24 h (ASM-074); App outbox releases on ACK only (ASM-079); Drone buffers until reconnect without flight closure (ADR-002).
- Private vs Public Path Separation: Farm telemetry and transporter traffic never cross center VPN; drone_object_ingress tier holds no endpoint in pilot (ASM-140).

div.div:
DIAGRAM LEGEND & CONNECTOR KEY:
---> Green/Teal Line: Telemetry & Sensor Path (MQTT/TLS direct to IoT Core public endpoint; bypasses centers and VPC)
---> Blue Line: Application & Logistics Flow (HTTPS TLS 1.2+ to CloudFront/Public API or via IPsec VPN to private endpoints)
---> Purple Line: Drone Mission & Imagery Path (Preloaded mission, private S3 multipart upload via object_storage endpoint)
---> Amber/Orange Line: WAN & Site-to-Site IPsec VPN (Dual tunnels over 100 Mbps WAN + cellular backup to TGW Hub)
---> Slate/Gray Line: Cloud Management & Monitoring (Route 53 Resolver, CloudWatch logs/metrics, session administration)
